links.note: Six-blank revision item; the first and governing blank is that employment in services has NOT risen to the same extent as production, which is 23773's description. The later blanks touch 23770, 23778, 23779, 23768/23769 and 23771 one each.

Four parts; the first asks how sectors are classified by ownership of enterprises, answered 'public and private' - 23782. DEFECT: the answer's second part defines the secondary sector as 'production of a commodity, mostly through the natural process', which is the PRIMARY sector's definition.

Five remedies asked and answered - canals for unirrigated land, cooperative marketing societies, low-interest bank credit, agro-based mills for off-season work, government procurement. That is 23777 item for item.

All four (tourist guide, vegetable vendor, cobbler, an airline) are service activities, so by the primary/secondary/tertiary scheme the stem names they are tertiary - 23770. DEFECT: the stored answer is internally inconsistent, classifying them across three different schemes at once (organised, unorganised, service, private).
The Surat table asks what percentage of the city's workers are in the unorganised sector - street workers, construction and domestic workers, and unregistered small workshops. 23779.

Whether the three-sector classification is useful, answered by what it lets us ascertain about each sector's contribution to GDP and per capita income. 23772's description names GDP as the measure used to compare sectors. 23773 is the sibling for the employment half of the same answer.
Asks explicitly why employment AND GDP are the two things to focus on per sector - 23773 is the concept that holds the contrast between a sector's output share and its employment share.
Lists adult occupations and classifies them; the answer puts one in primary, one in secondary and eleven in tertiary, so the tertiary concept is where the item's weight sits. 23770.
How the tertiary sector differs from the other two - it produces no goods but supports the other sectors through transport, communication, storage, banking and trade. 23770's description exactly.
Disguised unemployment with rural and urban examples - 23776, more people engaged than needed so removing some would not cut output.
Distinguishes open from disguised unemployment; the concept under test is disguised unemployment, 23776, since open unemployment has no concept of its own and serves as the contrast.

Rebuts the claim that the tertiary sector plays no significant role, arguing from its GDP share rising from about 35 per cent in 1973 to over 50 per cent in 2003 - 23774, the growth of services making the tertiary sector the largest producer.
The two kinds of people the service sector employs - highly skilled teachers and doctors against small shopkeepers and repair persons barely earning a living. 23775's unequal growth within services.

Exploitation in the unorganised sector - small scattered units outside government control, irregular and low-paid work, no overtime. 23779's description. 23781 covers the protections that would answer it, which this stem does not ask for.
Asks the classification by employment conditions, answered 'organised and unorganised'. Taken on 23778, the first of the pair and the registered-enterprise definition the scheme rests on.

Compares conditions in the two sectors; the comparison's substance is what the unorganised side lacks - no regular terms, no assured work - which is 23779. Its counterpart 23778 carries the item that names the scheme (qid:87418).
NREGA 2005's objective of 100 days of guaranteed employment is the employment-guarantee scheme named in 23777.
Compares private and public sector activities with local examples - 23782, grouping by who owns the assets and delivers the services. 23783 is why the government takes them up, which qid:87423 asks.
A table of well- and badly-managed organisations in the public and private sectors; the axis being tested is the ownership classification, 23782.
Examples of public sector activities AND why the government takes them up (welfare state, the poorest regions, services the private sector will not supply) - 23783.
How the public sector contributes to development, argued from government-owned assets and services such as Railways and Post Offices. 23783.

The stem names the issues on which unorganised workers need protection - wages, safety, health - and the answer works through each. That is 23781, the forms of protection. 23780 is the sibling identifying WHO needs protecting.

The Ahmedabad data to be tabulated is the organised/unorganised split of workers and income (11 lakh of 15 lakh workers unorganised), so 23779. The second half about generating employment reaches 23777.
Computes each sector's share of GDP for 1950 and 2000 and draws conclusions from the bar graph - the GDP measure used to compare sectors, 23772. The conclusion drawn touches 23774.

The five-yearly employment and unemployment survey behind India's employment figures is the methodological basis for comparing employment across sectors, 23773. DEFECT: the key is marked 'NREGA 2005', which is an Act, not a survey agency. The correct option is the NSSO.
Cotton as the natural product against textile, wheat flour and tomato sauce - 23768, goods produced by exploiting natural resources directly, as distinct from 23769's transformed products.
Who owns TISCO and Reliance Industries - the ownership classification, 23782. DEFECT: the key is marked 'a cooperative society'. Both are private companies, option (b); the key is wrong.
Underemployment as people working less than they are capable of is the same condition 23776 describes as disguised unemployment - the chapter uses the two terms for it.
The tertiary sector as India's largest producing sector - 23774, the growth of services. 23770 defines what the tertiary sector is; this item is about its rise to first place.
The central government undertaking the task of measuring GDP is stated in the GDP passage, 23772.
Life insurance as a service-sector activity - 23770, services supporting the other two sectors.
Bee keeping as the non-tertiary item against banking, teaching and call-centre work. The knowledge tested is what counts as tertiary, 23770.

The sector whose activities are not guided by the profit motive is the public sector, which is 23783's point - government provides what the private sector will not because there is no profit in it. 23782 is the bare ownership classification, which this stem goes beyond.
